chapter_seo_title: Li Huowang Confronts a Hidden Threat – Chapter 591 of Dao Gui Yi Xian
chapter_meta_description: A peaceful garden walk turns ominous when Li Huowang senses a hidden threat. The Chief Astrologer refuses to share the details, forcing Li Huowang to act alone. A tense chapter of political distrust and supernatural foreshadowing.
og_title: A Hidden Threat Lurks in the Imperial Gardens
og_description: Li Huowang’s brief respite in the palace is shattered when he senses unfinished business. With the Chief Astrologer’s trust withdrawn, Li Huowang must hunt the danger alone.
twitter_title: The Siming’s Shadow Looms Over Great Liang
twitter_description: Li Huowang’s fragile peace in the palace is broken. The Chief Astrologer warns him that he is “no longer just himself.” A masterful quiet chapter.

lore_anchors.definition: A high-ranking official overseeing celestial and supernatural matters for the imperial court; his role is to “monitor the heavens” and manage threats that cross between the political and cosmic realms.

The underground energy channels that determine a dynasty’s fate and legitimacy in Chinese geomancy; in the novel, the Mandate of Heaven is a stolen fragment of divine power held up at a terrible price.
Historical slang for erotic or bawdy folk opera performances, often considered lowbrow entertainment.
A government-backed law enforcement body that hunts rogue cultivators and manages supernatural disasters; its name puns on “overseeing the heavens.”
